title: Pair the hard-won doctrine with the technique
summary: The most transferable lessons of a maintained system are often its invariants and doctrine, not just its API usage: providers return data and are never executed; evidence is not acceptance; paths are grants to verified objects; absent fails closed. A sphere that captures only technique robs the next model of the 'why' that makes the technique stick and stops it breaking the contract.
evidence_note: The bashqueues build deliberately included the doctrine layer (typed stdout, data-not-shell, evidence-not-acceptance, fail-closed, versioned schemas, path locks) because it is where an LLM-authored change goes wrong most.
invariants: Record the invariants/doctrine of the domain alongside the mechanics.
Teach the 'why' next to the 'how' so a model applies the rule rather than only the shape.
Explicitly separate evidence from acceptance in whatever you author into a sphere.
Absent/unknown is a deniable first-class state, never a silent allow.
